Section B
Answer any three questions.
Each question is introduced by stimulus material. In your answer you may refer to this material and/or
to other examples that you have studied.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify two reasons why people become entrepreneurs.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two benefits that an MNC can bring to its host country.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Analyse how a government could encourage the consumption of merit goods.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss whether or not private sector firms are likely to charge lower prices than public sector
firms.

text: Vietnam has a high number of female entrepreneurs. Some of their firms have grown and now
compete with foreign multinational companies (MNCs) and public sector firms. The Vietnamese
government encourages MNCs to locate in Vietnam as a host country. It also intervenes in the
economy to encourage the consumption of merit goods.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define a minimum price.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two advantages of capital‑intensive production.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Analyse why low‑income farmers are likely to have low living standards.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss whether or not a government subsidy on the export of sugar will help it achieve its
macroeconomic aims.

text: In 2019, India became the world’s largest producer of sugar. Sugar cane is grown in the country
by a large number of mainly low‑income farmers. They sell sugar cane to mills which process the
sugar cane into sugar. Processing the sugar cane is more capital‑intensive than growing it. The
Indian government sets a minimum price for sugar cane and subsidises the export of sugar.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two reasons why someone may choose to become a doctor.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Analyse how advances in technology may improve the current account balance on a country’s
balance of payments.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss whether or not a country with a high population growth rate is likely to experience a
high economic growth rate.

text: Safiye Ali became the first female doctor in Turkey in 1923. By 2020, 40% of Turkish doctors were
women. Over this period, labour productivity increased. Turkey also experienced advances in
technology, a change in the current account balance on its balance of payments and a significant
increase in the size of its population.

text: Serbia is the world’s second largest producer of raspberries, a product with elastic demand.
Consumers experience the economic problem when buying raspberries. Few raspberry farm
workers are members of trade unions. Membership of trade unions in Serbia had fallen to 20% of
all workers by 2020. In that year, Serbia had more state pensioners than workers.
